dedupe_keys.name: transimhub unified air ground simulation platform

description: TranSimHub is an open-source simulation platform for air-ground collaborative intelligence in urban traffic, in which unmanned aerial vehicles and ground vehicles, signals and sensors perceive, communicate and act together. It is developed by the Traffic-Alpha group led by Maonan Wang with co-authors from Hong Kong, mainland China, France and Stanford, and described in a 2025 arXiv paper. The platform runs ground traffic in SUMO and adds aerial agents, synchronised multi-view rendering in RGB, depth and semantic segmentation so aerial and ground views agree, information exchange between the two domains, and a causal scene editor for controllable and counterfactual scenarios with weather, emergency events and dynamic obstacles. Coverage is generic: any SUMO road network. Access: Python package and source on GitHub with online documentation; it requires Python 3.9 or later and a SUMO installation. Licence and cost: Apache-2.0, free (the paper is CC BY 4.0). Caveats: aimed at perception and learning research, not airspace or air traffic management, drone dynamics and communication are simplified, and the project is young. It supports digital twin experiments, emergency response scenarios such as drone-assisted incident management, and network flow control studies. It builds on the SUMO platform catalogued here.
